# <span id="aanchor427"></span> Hydrocarbon Properties

Accessing this form requires **System Process – System Information** privileges.

Use the Hydrocarbon Properties (HC) Editor to specify physical constants for various analytical properties of hydrocarbon components such as water, CO, ethane and cyclopentane. You can also specify the source of each set of constants. These values are used in quality source calculations for determining values such as liquid volume %, heating value, mass % and density. They are also used for calculating component volumes and component mass on meters and tickets.

FLOWCAL allows the creation and editing of sets of constants as new standards are published. New records may also be required if a contract calls for a value outside of the published standards which needs to be used in calculations.

By default, a set of constants labeled "US Units 2003" is applied to all meters and liquid quality sources in a system from the beginning of time to 01/01/2009 00:00:00. A set of constants labeled "US Units 2009" is applied from 01/01/2009 00:00:00 to 01/01/2017 00:00:00. A set of constants labeled “US Units 2016” is applied from 01/01/2017 00:00:00 until the end of time.

Base pressure and base temperature at which the values were measured are also given, as is the gas constant and the source document from which the constants were taken.

Each set of physical constants can be assigned to a meter, a ticket or to a quality source for a given date and time range.

<div class="exception" style="margin-left: 0;">

#### Distribution Notes for GPA 2145-16

GPA 2145-16 is the source document for most of the values for the two FLOWCAL default sets, US Units 2016 and SI Units 2016 at 15C.

- The heating value of water has been omitted because water does not contribute to combustion.
- The heating value of hydrogen sulfide has been omitted because it is not a saleable component of the gas/liquid product.
- Liquid densities for ethylene published in the current revision are given for the liquid state at the normal boiling point, not at 60°F/15°C. GPA is discussing an appropriate density that can be used at these standard temperatures.
- All properties for butylenes have been omitted. FLOWCAL has not previously included these properties. If butylene values were previously entered in FLOWCAL, they will need to be added to the current template as well.
- Any of the above properties can be added manually via the Hydrocarbon Properties editor.
- These sets do not include the 25 new published components.

</div>

 

<div class="procedure">

To create a new set of constants in the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Hydrocarbon Properties**.

2.  Select **File** \> **New**.

    The characteristics defined for the set of constants selected prior to choosing New will be carried over to a new configuration by default.

3.  Enter a label.

4.  Make changes as applicable.

5.  Click **Save**.

Once created, the Hydrocarbon Properties configuration can be edited as needed, but it cannot be deleted.

</div>

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Hydrocarbon Properties Editor Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available in the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor:

- **Label** - Contains a list of existing Hydrocarbon Properties configurations.
- **Base Pressure/Temperature** - The base temperature and pressure associated with the extended characteristics defined by a Hydrocarbon Properties configuration are displayed and may be edited.
- **Constants (Density of Water, Density of Air, Univ. Gas Constant)** - This is where the constants may be defined for the density of water, density of air, and the Universal Gas Constant used in the derivation of the extended characteristics for each component. The density of water defined here is not used in the calculation standards such as Table A. Each one uses the density of water defined by the standard to calculate the correct results as prescribed by the standard
- **Compounds** - Applicable standards. Allows for different characteristic values to be set up per component based on TP-17 characteristic values.
- **Columns** - Extended component characteristics. Several characteristics are displayed for each component:
  - Component name (read-only)

  - Source document from which the characteristics were derived

    The source may be a published standard, company literature or any other data source. Once the source for the data is entered in the HC Property Source Document Editor, it can be used for specifying the source document on the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor.

  - Molar mass (g/mol)

  - Relative density as an ideal gas

  - Absolute density as a liquid (in lbm/gal or Kg/m3)

  - Volume ratio (in ft3/gal)

  - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/ft3 or MJ/m3)

  - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/gal)

  - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/lbm or MJ/Kg)

  - Gross heating value of fuel as a liquid (in Btu/gal or MJ/m3)

  - Gross heating value of fuel as a liquid (in Btu/lbm or MJ/Kg)

  - Net heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/ft3 or MJ/m3)

  - Vapor pressure (in psia or kPa)

  - Heat of vaporization (in Btu/lb or KJ/kgm)

  - Critical temperature (in °F or °C)

  - Critical pressure (in psia or kPa)

  - Normal boiling point (in °F at 14.696 psia or K at 101.325 kPa)

  - Characteristic volume (ft3/lb-mol or m3/kmol)

  - Acentric factor
- **Show** - The selection made here determines which class of components is displayed in the grid, allowing for components to be more easily viewed or edited.
- **Find** - Perform quick value and text searches within the HC Properties data table grid. For example: You can search for a value, such as 58.122, or for text, such as "Ethane". To activate the find functionality, press **Ctrl+F** or go to **File** \> **Find**.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Tools">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Tool Menu Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Tools">

The following options are available in the Tools menu:

- **Change Decimal Positions** - Specify the discrimination for each characteristic in a given configuration. Each applicable standard has separate settings, and the settings which the editor controls are determined by which standard was selected when the form was opened. You must be in edit mode to change the discrimination, and the number of decimals specified for a characteristic determines the number of decimals to which its values are displayed and editable on the main form.
- **Manage Source Documents** - Open the [Hydrocarbon Property Source Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/HC%20Property%20Source%20Document%20Editor.md).
- **System HC Properties** - Launch the [Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor](Hydrocarbon%20Property%20Time%20Frame%20Editor.md).

</div>
